A particle $P$ moves with constant acceleration $(2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. At time $t=0$, $P$ has speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. At time $t=3\,\mathrm{s}$, $P$ has velocity $(-6\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Find the value of $u$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$-6\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}=\mathbf{u}+3(2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$ M1 A1
$\Rightarrow \mathbf{u}=-12\mathbf{i}+16\mathbf{j}$ A1 cso
$\Rightarrow u=\sqrt{(-12)^2+16^2}=20$ M1 A1

questions.stem:
A bench consists of a plank which is resting in a horizontal position on two thin vertical legs. The plank is modelled as a uniform rod $PS$ of length 2.4 m and mass 20 kg. The legs at $Q$ and $R$ are 0.4 m from each end of the plank, as shown in Figure 1.

Two pupils, Arthur and Beatrice, sit on the plank. Arthur has mass 60 kg and sits at the middle of the plank and Beatrice has mass 40 kg and sits at the end $P$. The plank remains horizontal and in equilibrium. By modelling the pupils as particles, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the magnitude of the normal reaction between the plank and the leg at $Q$ and the magnitude of the normal reaction between the plank and the leg at $R$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
$C+D=120g$
$M(Q)$, $80g\times 0.8-40g\times 0.4=D\times 1.6$ M1 A1
solving M1 A1
$C=90g$; $D=30g$ M1, A1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Beatrice stays sitting at $P$ but Arthur now moves and sits on the plank at the point $X$. Given that the plank remains horizontal and in equilibrium, and that the magnitude of the normal reaction between the plank and the leg at $Q$ is now twice the magnitude of the normal reaction between the plank and the leg at $R$,

(b) find the distance $QX$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$2F+F=40g+20g+60g$ M1 A1
$M(Q)$, $60gx+20g\times 0.8=40g\times 0.4+F\times 1.6$ M1 A1
solving M1
$QX=x=\frac{16}{15}\,\mathrm{m}=1.07\,\mathrm{m}$ A1

questions.stem:
A small package of mass 1.1 kg is held in equilibrium on a rough plane by a horizontal force. The plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha=\frac{3}{4}$. The force acts in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope of the plane and has magnitude $P$ newtons, as shown in Figure 2.

The coefficient of friction between the package and the plane is 0.5 and the package is modelled as a particle. The package is in equilibrium and on the point of slipping down the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw, on Figure 2, all the forces acting on the package, showing their directions clearly.
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) (i) Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the package and the plane.
(ii) Find the value of $P$.
(11)
parts.mark_scheme:
$F=\frac{1}{2}R$ B1
$(\uparrow)$, $R\cos\alpha+F\sin\alpha=mg$ M1 A2
$R=\frac{1.1g}{\cos\alpha+\frac{1}{2}\sin\alpha}=9.8\,\mathrm{N}$ M1 A1
$(\rightarrow)$, $P+\frac{1}{2}R\cos\alpha=R\sin\alpha$ M1 A2
$P=R(\sin\alpha-\frac{1}{2}\cos\alpha)$ M1
$=1.96$ A1

questions.stem: Two forces, $(4\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$ and $(p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N}$, act on a particle $P$ of mass $m$ kg. The resultant of the two forces is $\mathbf{R}$. Given that $\mathbf{R}$ acts in a direction which is parallel to the vector $(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the angle between $\mathbf{R}$ and the vector $\mathbf{j}$,
(3)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given also that $q=1$ and that $P$ moves with an acceleration of magnitude $8\sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$,

(c) find the value of $m$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
$q=1 \Rightarrow p=-2$ B1
$\Rightarrow \mathbf{R}=2\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}$ M1
$\Rightarrow |\mathbf{R}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-4)^2}=\sqrt{20}$ M1 A1 f.t.
$\sqrt{20}=m\times 8\sqrt{5}$ M1 A1 f.t.
$\Rightarrow m=\frac{1}{4}$ A1 cao

angle is $153.4^\circ$ A1

The mass of block $Q$ is 5 kg and the mass of block $R$ is 10 kg. The scale pan hangs at rest and the system is released from rest. By modelling the blocks as particles, ignoring air resistance and assuming the motion is uninterrupted, find

(ii) the tension in the string,
